newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU may reassess wheat exports to Africa-official.
newsitem.headline: EU may reassess wheat exports to Africa-official.

text.p: The European Union may reassess plans to sell its wheat to a target group of African nations after EU firms failed to show proof of contracts by the November 15 deadline, a senior EU grain official told Reuters.
The official said the issue may come up for discussion at next week's meeting of the EU grain committee in Brussels.
But he stressed that it was difficult to say what action the EU might take in the face of volatile world prices.
"We are bound to reassess the supply situation of African nations but it is hard to say what we may do," the official said.
"We may wait for things to cool down a bit," he said, referring to recent fluctuations in world wheat prices.

Exporters who had applied for long-term licences to sell EU wheat to a target group of African nations did not show proof of contract by the agreed deadline on November 15, France's grain office ONIC said earlier.
Traders had applied for licences valid until June 30, 1997 under the so-called article nine that required traders to show proof of contract to get their refunds.
The licences carried a special refund of 12 Ecus per tonne until December and 19 Ecus from December onwards. The special refunds were aimed at providing relief to hard pressed African nations.
The EU usually exports between 800,000 tonnes and one million tonnes of wheat each year to the target group of African countries.
Under the long-term scheme traders had applied for licences to export between 350,000 and one million tonnes of soft wheat.
But recent increases in regular EU wheat export refunds had removed the incentive for traders to use the special refunds applying to wheat exports to Africa, traders said.
When the EU set the special refunds, world wheat prices were still firm. But since then the EU stepped up its rebates on wheat exports to keep pace with falling world prices.
"It was bad timing. We did it (the special refund) when the market really slumped," the official reckoned.
A rally in U.S. wheat futures on Tuesday and Wednesday however monentarily eased pressure for lower EU subsidies.
On Thursday the Commission lowered the refund offered on wheat exports to 15.97 Ecus from 22.35 Ecus.
The official said the Commission's position was to keep pace with world prices but that it was very difficult to say where these prices were heading.

"U.S. soft red and hard red winter wheat has firmed and the (EU) rebate came down. Maybe next week prices will slump again and we may head the other way. No one knows," he said. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
